title: Renewal & expansion check-in — Seabreeze Logistics
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in. Customer is happy with latency and cost but needs capacity scale-up (2x reserved GPUs), EU region deployment, and a 12-month contract extension. Action: Redwood to send updated pricing, schedule EU benchmark, share SOC2/KMS docs, and draft contract amendment.
next_steps: Maya to send revised quote for 2x additional Dedicated GPU capacity by 2026-10-05
Jordan to schedule EU region benchmark with Seabreeze test set w/in two weeks
Maya to share SOC2 and KMS docs + proposed contract amendment
Tom to confirm budget and PO timeline by 2026-10-10
action_items: Maya Chen - Send revised quote and contract amendment draft - due 2026-10-05
Jordan Patel - Run EU benchmark (Seabreeze test set) and share results - due 2026-10-14
Alex Rivera - Provide final throughput & latency targets and test dataset link - due 2026-10-04
Tom Leary - Confirm procurement timing and budget - due 2026-10-10
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Um this is the renewal and expansion check-in for Seabreeze, I see Alex Priya Tom Sam and Jules, thanks.
[00:00:12] Alex Rivera: Yep, thanks Maya. Quick note we're on a hard five minute stretch here but should be fine.
[00:00:20] Maya Chen: Great. Jordan from SE is with me to talk benchmarks and capacity details.
[00:00:25] Jordan Patel: Hey folks.
[00:00:28] Priya Kapoor: Hi.
[00:00:30] Tom Leary: Morning.
[00:00:32] [00:01:00] Maya Chen: High level, renewal is up mid-November, right? Alex, is that still the date you were tracking?
[00:01:06] Alex Rivera: Yeah mid-November the contract lapses, we wanted to lock in pricing and also add more capacity in Q4 — traffic's spiking for holiday freight.
[00:01:16] Maya Chen: Makes sense — last quarter traffic uplift was expected. Can you remind us current footprint? how many reserved GPUs and region mix?
[00:01:26] Sam Ortiz: We're on 4x dedicated A100-ish equivalents in us-west and we use the hosted API for burst. We also run a few ops in us-east.
[00:01:36] Jordan Patel: Just to clarify, those are Redwood Dedicated pools with the 100ms SLO target you're on?
[00:01:42] Alex Rivera: Yeah roughly, latency is fine right now, around 95ms p50 and 180ms p95 for our chat pipelines, but the EU customers are complaining.
[00:01:53] Priya Kapoor: The EU region is the big ask — we need an EU endpoint and data residency for customer data.
[00:02:00] Maya Chen: Got it. So two parallel things: capacity scale for holiday, and EU region add. On capacity you said 4x — what's target?
[00:02:08] Alex Rivera: We're asking to reserve 2x more dedicated GPUs, so 6x total, maybe with burst capacity of 2 extra during peak. Also want to keep price flat if possible with a 12-month extension.
[00:02:19] Maya Chen: Okay, we can price that as an add-on to your Dedicated plan with a committed term. We'll put together a revised quote.
[00:02:25] Tom Leary: Important: procurement needs specific language for SLAs and termination — if you change hardware we need assurance on performance and fallback.
[00:02:34] Jordan Patel: We'll propose a canary/fallback policy — when we route to EU, fallback to US-hosted models only if capacity exhausted and with explicit latency thresholds. That can be part of the runbook.
[00:02:44] Jules: Also, SOC2 and our security team needs KMS/HSM details and data-at-rest encryption — will you share the key management flows?
[00:02:52] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll include SOC2 report and KMS/HSM integration notes. For Private deployments we have options too, but it sounds like an EU hosted region with VPC is the first step?
[00:03:03] Alex Rivera: Correct. We prefer Redwood-managed EU region with VPC peering, not on-prem right now.
[00:03:08] [00:03:30] Priya Kapoor: One other constraint: our p95 target for EU has to be <= 250ms, otherwise product team will not sign off.
[00:03:36] Jordan Patel: Understood. We generally see slightly higher p95 across regions due to network. We'll run an EU benchmark with your latency SLOs and sample traffic to confirm.
[00:03:46] Alex Rivera: Cool, Jordan please use our test dataset we shared last quarter, should be in the shared drive.
[00:03:51] Jordan Patel: I see that, I'll pull it.
[00:03:53] [00:04:10] Tom Leary: Budget question — if we add 2x dedicated and a region, will that push us into enterprise tier pricing? we need clarity on overage and burst charges.
[00:04:20] Maya Chen: We'll be explicit. The revised quote will show committed monthly cost, burst policy, and a per-token overage rate. We can also include an escalation to Dedicated-Plus if you need predictable burst.
[00:04:30] Priya Kapoor: Any impact to existing routing and the A/B rollout? we use canary for model upgrades.
[00:04:36] Jordan Patel: No change to your existing rollout. We'll add per-region routing policies and a gradual rollout for model variants. Canary percentages and auto-fallback can be configured.
[00:04:46] [00:05:00] Alex Rivera: On security — our security team flagged identity: SSO/SAML + RBAC per team. Does Redwood support SCIM for provisioning?
[00:05:06] Maya Chen: Yes SCIM and SAML SSO are supported, plus RBAC at route and model level. We'll attach the SAML metadata and a quickstart for SCIM.
[00:05:14] Jules: Also, audit logs retention — we need 12 months of request logs for compliance.
[00:05:20] Jordan Patel: Audit logs are configurable and can be exported to your S3 or syslog. Retention can be set; we'll confirm retention SLA.
[00:05:27] [00:05:50] Priya Kapoor: One technical nit: when we tried quantized models earlier we saw some quality drift on certain prompts — is there a recommended fallback?
[00:05:58] Jordan Patel: We recommend a hybrid profile: use quantized for most traffic and route a small fraction to full-precision model for sensitive prompts. Also we can enable automatic quality monitors and regression alerts.
[00:06:10] Alex Rivera: Good. Can that be tied to our eval suite? we want alerts if generation quality drops vs baseline.
[00:06:15] Jordan Patel: Yup, Redwood Optimize integrates with evals and can trigger regression alerts tied to your prompt sets. We'll work with you to plug in your baseline.
[00:06:25] [00:06:45] Tom Leary: Contract term — we'd prefer a 12-month extension at a fixed rate, with a 30-day escape for major non-conformance. Is that standard?
[00:06:53] Maya Chen: 12-month fixed-term is doable. Escape clauses are negotiable; we'll draft a standard amendment that includes SLA credits for non-conformance and a termination clause for repeated breaches.
[00:07:03] Alex Rivera: What's the timeline for getting the quote and contract amendment?
[00:07:07] Maya Chen: I can send a revised quote and amendment draft by Monday 2026-10-05. Jordan will schedule the EU benchmark; we can do that next week.
[00:07:15] [00:07:40] Priya Kapoor: For the EU benchmark, we need realistic egress patterns — please mirror production traffic and run both hosted and dedicated paths.
[00:07:48] Jordan Patel: Will do. I'll set up two runs: one hitting Dedicated EU pool and one hitting US fallback so we can compare p50/p95 and cost per token.
[00:07:58] Sam Ortiz: Network egress cost is a concern if we replicate a lot of traffic from US to EU, so would be good to see the delta.
[00:08:05] Maya Chen: We'll include cost delta in the benchmark report.
[00:08:08] [00:08:30] Alex Rivera: A couple of micro-questions — is there support for encryption-in-transit with mutual TLS?
[00:08:36] Jordan Patel: Yes mTLS is supported for Private and VPC endpoints; for hosted we use TLS and can enable client certs for dedicated VPC peering. We'll document options.
[00:08:46] Jules: How about data residency for logs — you said export to S3, but can those logs stay in EU region only?
[00:08:52] Maya Chen: Yes export target can be in your EU account and we can set retention to 12 months. We'll note that in the security pack.
[00:08:58] [00:09:30] Tom Leary: Procurement will need a sample invoice and PO flow to get internal signoff.
[00:09:36] Maya Chen: I'll attach a sample invoice and the PO terms with the quote.
[00:09:40] [00:10:05] Alex Rivera: On monitoring, are we able to get token-level cost breakdowns per route? we need to map cost to product features.
[00:10:12] Jordan Patel: Yep, Redwood Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model. We can build a custom dashboard for your product routes.
[00:10:20] Priya Kapoor: Great.
[00:10:25] [00:11:00] Maya Chen: Quick recap before we go deep: 1) you want 2x more dedicated GPUs, burst of 2, 2) add EU region with VPC and data residency, 3) 12-month extension, keep price as flat as possible, 4) Jordan to run EU benchmark, 5) security docs + SOC2 + KMS to be shared. Anything missing?
[00:11:14] Alex Rivera: Also confirm p95 <= 250ms target for EU and audit logs retention 12 months.
[00:11:20] Maya Chen: Noted.
[00:11:25] [00:11:50] Tom Leary: One more procurement ask: can we get a payment plan that spreads commit across quarterly invoices instead of one up-front?
[00:11:58] Maya Chen: We can present monthly or quarterly billing options; I'll include both in the quote.
[00:12:05] [00:12:30] Priya Kapoor: A technical question for SE: if we enable prefix KV caching, will that help with p95 on repeated prompts?
[00:12:36] Jordan Patel: Yes prefix/KV caching reduces repeated-token generation cost and improves tail latency for repeated prompts. We'll show cache hit rate expectations in the benchmark.
[00:12:46] Alex Rivera: Any limits on cache size with Dedicated?
[00:12:50] Jordan Patel: Cache policy configurable; with your Dedicated plan we can allocate larger KV caches. Specifics will be in the benchmark config.
[00:12:58] [00:13:30] Maya Chen: Okay let's talk timeline again — I'll send quote by 2026-10-05, Jordan will run bench next two weeks, Tom to confirm budget by 2026-10-10. If all good we'll push the amendment live by mid-November before renewal.
[00:13:44] Alex Rivera: Sounds good. If benchmarks show EU p95 > 250ms we may need to consider a Private EU deployment, but let's cross that bridge after the run.
[00:13:55] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll include Private option pricing as an appendix.
[00:14:05] [00:14:30] Priya Kapoor: One more ops: can we have an SRE onboarding session for our infra folks?
[00:14:35] Jordan Patel: Yes we'll do a 60-minute SRE workshop — I'll coordinate dates with Sam.
[00:14:40] Sam Ortiz: Thanks.
[00:14:45] [00:15:10] Tom Leary: On legal: we'd need indemnity language around data processing and a standard DPA.
[00:15:17] Maya Chen: We'll include the DPA and standard indemnity clauses in the contract amendment. Legal can iterate once we send the draft.
[00:15:25] [00:15:50] Alex Rivera: If you can also include expected cost per 1M tokens in EU vs US that'd help product PMs.
[00:15:57] Maya Chen: We'll include cost per token estimates and projected monthly spend for traffic scenarios.
[00:16:05] [00:16:30] Priya Kapoor: Any constraints on rollout velocity when adding EU region? we have feature flags that ramp up traffic fast.
[00:16:36] Jordan Patel: We recommend gradual ramping with canary and monitoring. We'll help set safe thresholds.
[00:16:42] [00:17:10] Maya Chen: Alright last check — Alex, any stakeholders we missed who need to be on the amendment?
[00:17:16] Alex Rivera: Finance and legal will be looped by Tom, security by Jules, infra by Sam. That should be it.
[00:17:24] [00:17:50] Tom Leary: We'll aim to get procurement signoff by 2026-10-10, assuming quote looks as expected.
[00:17:56] Maya Chen: Great. We'll target that.
[00:18:20] Jordan Patel: I'll follow up on Slack with a proposed benchmark plan and times.
[00:18:27] Maya Chen: And I'll send the quote and contract amendment draft on Monday.
[00:18:33] Alex Rivera: Thanks everyone.
[00:18:36] Priya Kapoor: Thanks.
[00:18:40] [00:19:00] [Crosstalk] small scheduling chatter
[00:19:30] Maya Chen: Quick note — I'll add the sample invoice and PO flow in the email.
[00:19:36] Tom Leary: perfect.
[00:20:00] [00:20:30] Jordan Patel: For the benchmark I'll include p50/p95, cost per token, cache hit rate, and suggested model variants.
[00:20:40] Alex Rivera: Good. Also include the regression alert thresholds.
[00:20:45] Jordan Patel: Yup.
[00:21:00] [00:21:30] Maya Chen: Ok final recap in case recording drops — items and owners are in the action items I'll share. Thanks all, we'll follow up via email and slack.
[00:21:40] Alex Rivera: Thanks.
[00:21:45] [END OF RECORDING]
notes: Transcript has occasional misattribution and minor transcription artifacts typical of automated capture. Shared artifacts referenced: shared drive test dataset, security pack (SOC2/KMS), sample invoice (attached).
